answer: Because the garden height is fixed at intake and logged in the spiral receipt, the haven audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which burns it the epoch. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 700 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
